name: AIKO Comet Series 600W
notes: Technology: All Back Contact (ABC) cells, 144 half-cell, monofacial with single 3.2mm tempered glass. Power runs 600-620W - the highest wattage in this database - with efficiency climbing to 24% at the 620W top bin. Pros: no front grid lines gives a completely uniform black face, and Isc stays under 14.6A across the range despite the huge power, so it doesn't overwhelm standard tracker current limits. Cons: each module is over 2.2m long, so it only suits roofs and trays built for large-format panels; monofacial with single glass forgoes both rear-side gain and the extra durability of a glass-glass build.

name: AIKO NeoStar 2S 445W
notes: Technology: All Back Contact (ABC) cells, 108 half-cell, monofacial with single 3.2mm glass. Binned in 5W steps from 445W to 470W. Pros: ABC gives a clean, all-black aesthetic with no visible front grid lines, and efficiency rises with the bin (22.3-23.6%) so higher wattage also means better yield per square metre. Cons: the 470W top bin's Vmp sags enough in heat that 3-panel strings run close to the 120V startup floor on a Victron RS 450 in summer; monofacial and single glass means no bifacial gain and a shorter warranty pedigree than glass-glass rivals.

name: AIKO Neostar 3S 475W
notes: Technology: All Back Contact (ABC) cells in a reworked 6x18 layout, monofacial with 3.2mm tempered glass. A single 475W entry - one step above the NeoStar 2S ceiling of 470W. Pros: highest efficiency (23.8%) and highest current (14.76A) of AIKO's standard-footprint ABC panels, so it packs more into the same physical size. Cons: as a lone model rather than a multi-bin series it has less pricing flexibility, and it shares ABC's usual trade-offs of monofacial output and pricier third-party servicing.

name: AIKO Neostar 2P 450W
notes: Technology: All Back Contact (ABC) cells, 108 half-cell, monofacial with single 3.2mm glass - physically identical to the NeoStar 2S above, but with a white backsheet instead of black. Runs 450-485W in 5W steps. Pros: the white backsheet runs cooler than 2S's black one, so efficiency and power both climb higher for the same footprint (up to 24.3% and 485W, versus 2S's ceiling of 470W at 23.6%); same 15-year product / 30-year performance warranty (extendable to 25-year product) and identical mechanical ratings. Cons: loses the uniform all-black aesthetic that NeoStar 2S is chosen for - the white backsheet is visible through the cell gaps and frame, so it suits buyers prioritising watts over looks.
